companies.funding_notes: BranchTrack (branchtrack.com), Riga-founded scenario-based training simulation builder. Also won $10k How To Web 'Best Startup' prize (2015, not counted). No later rounds reported.

companies.name: Reinfer
companies.description: Re:infer takes the communications streams you receive and turns them into something you can automate a business process against.
companies.funding_notes: Re:infer (reinfer.io), UCL AI-lab spinout (2015) turning business communications into structured data. $3.5m (£2.5m) seed led by Touchstone Innovations (Feb 2018); company announced $7.6m raised to date in Feb 2022 alongside a ~£3.2m seed follow-on led by Crane (some reports date a Crane-led ~$4.5m round to 2020 — likely the same money). amount_raised uses the company's $7.6m cumulative figure; TechCrunch later said 'a little more than $11m'. Acquired by UiPath Aug 2022 (undisclosed).

companies.name: Grover
companies.description: Reinventing consumption with a simple, on-demand subscription model for all the products you love.

investors: Mirae Asset-LG Electronics New Growth Fund

companies.funding_notes: Grover (grover.com, formerly ByeBuy), Berlin consumer-tech rental/subscription platform. Equity-only figures listed; excludes large debt facilities (€25m 2018, €30m Varengold 2019, €15m Kreos 2021, $220m Fasanara 2022, etc.; company cites >€1.4bn total financing incl. debt). Series C valued it >$1bn. 2024 €50m 'bridge' instrument type not specified (may be convertible). 2025 court-backed restructuring reportedly shifted majority equity to creditors. Mixed EUR/USD so amount_raised blank (~€119m + $110m).
notable_investors: Mirae Asset-LG Electronics New Growth Fund

companies.name: Monese
companies.description: Monese is a digital banking option that provides mobile-only, multi-currency accounts in countries across the European Economic Area.
companies.funding_notes: Monese (monese.com), London/Estonian-founded mobile banking app (founder Norris Koppel). Totals reported: $15.8m after Series A (2017), $76m after Series B (2018), $162m after Series C first close (2021), $208m after HSBC's $35m (2022) — amount_raised uses that reported $208m cumulative (includes early seed/crowd money). Series C reported as $90m by TechCrunch (£65.8m headline by Deal Lite). Acquired in a rescue deal by Pockit in Oct 2024 (HSBC wrote off its stake).

companies.name: Spoke
companies.description: Properly made clothes that really fit, direct from the workshop.
companies.funding_notes: Spoke (spoke-london.com), London D2C menswear/trousers brand (founder Ben Farren) — not Spoke messaging. $1.8m late seed (Jan 2017; total then just over $3m incl. earlier Seedcamp-era money); €9.7m (~£8.5m) Series B led by BGF (Oct 2019); £5m 2022 round mostly Seedrs crowdfunding (£4.71m from 1,579 investors) plus existing VCs. A £4m Nov 2017 Series A appears only in databases. Mixed USD/EUR/GBP so amount_raised blank.

companies.name: Trussle
companies.description: Simpler way to get a mortgage.
companies.funding_notes: Trussle (trussle.com), London online mortgage broker (founder Ishaan Malhi). £1.1m seed (2016), £4.5m Series A (2017), £13.6m Series B (2018), £7.5m 2020 raise with Rabo Frontier Ventures (round label not stated; recorded here as Series B extension). Acquired by Better (Better.com) announced July 2021; trussle.com later rebranded to Better.co.uk.

companies.name: Revolut
companies.description: Revolut is a financial services company that specializes in mobile banking, card payments, money remittance, and foreign exchange.
companies.funding_notes: Revolut (revolut.com), London-founded global fintech/'superapp' (CEO Nik Storonsky). Seedcamp invested Feb 2015; seed £1.5m ($2.3m) led by Balderton (Jul 2015), extended to $4.8m total by Feb 2016. Primary equity Series A–E sums to ~$1.71B (Series E at $33B). Later 2024 ($45B) and Nov 2025 ($75B, led by Coatue/Greenoaks/Dragoneer/Fidelity) transactions were employee/secondary share sales and excluded; Crowdcube campaigns folded into the Series A figure.

companies.name: Marcopolo Learning
companies.description: Reimagining children's media
companies.funding_notes: New York-based MarcoPolo Learning (marcopololearning.com) makes early-childhood education apps and video. Raised ~$1M from angels in May 2013 (SEC Form D shows $740K sold of a $2M offering, first sale 2013-05-31), then an $8.5M round in April 2017 led by Boat Rocker Ventures with Horizons Ventures, Seedcamp and DST Global partners; ImpactAlpha labels it Series A (VentureBeat/FinSMEs call it its first round).

companies.name: Hubble
companies.description: Making renting office space easy
companies.funding_notes: Hubble (hubblehq.com, legal entity Spacious Ltd, formerly Spacious/HubbleHQ) is a London flexible-office marketplace founded 2014 by Entrepreneur First alumni; not the telescope or Hubble Network. Rounds: £500K seed (2014, Spire lead, Seedcamp), £1.2M (2017), €4.6M Series A (2019, JLL Spark lead), £2M Series A follow-on (2021, Pi Labs lead); company said total raised £10M by July 2021. Mixed GBP/EUR so amount_raised left blank; a 2022 ~£7-8M round appears only in databases (not included). Acquired by Yardi in January 2025.

companies.name: Property Partner
companies.description: Property crowdfunding platform and trading exchange.
companies.funding_notes: Property Partner (propertypartner.co) was a London residential property crowdfunding platform with a share-trading exchange, founded by Daniel Gandesha. Raised £150K angel (Feb 2014), £1.25M seed led by Octopus with Seedcamp (Sep 2014), £5.2M Series A led by Index Ventures (Mar 2015), and a £15.9M Series B led by Octopus with Index and Dawn (Mar 2016). The Series B included a £3M SVB venture-debt facility, so it's recorded as £12.9M equity; total equity is ~£19.5M (reported total funding £22.5M including debt).

companies.name: Lodgify
companies.description: Create your own vacation rental website
companies.funding_notes: Lodgify (lodgify.com) is a Barcelona-based vacation-rental website/booking SaaS founded 2012 by Dennis Klett and Marco De Gregorio. Raised €1.4M in April 2016 led by Nauta (total €2M at that point, so ~€0.6M earlier from angels incl. HOWZAT/Hitchen/Zeller) and a $5M Series A in July 2018 (total $7.3M per TechCrunch). Mixed EUR/USD so amount_raised left blank; total reported $7.3M.

companies.name: Reedsy
companies.description: A community of top publishing professionals to create amazing books.
companies.funding_notes: Reedsy (reedsy.com) is a London marketplace connecting authors with vetted editors, designers and marketers. Got €30K from Seedcamp and DC Thomson in 2014 while raising a €500K round; TechCrunch (Apr 2015) reported an undisclosed 'initial round of financing' with DN Capital, Kima, DC Thomson, Seedcamp and angels, not labelled seed. A ~€1.1M EU (EIC/SME Instrument) grant in 2016 appears only in a database and is not included as unverified.

companies.name: BridgeU
companies.description: Data-driven university and careers guidance to empower schools
companies.funding_notes: BridgeU (bridge-u.com) is a London university and careers guidance platform for international schools, founded by Lucy Stonehill and Hywel Carver; Seedcamp backed it in spring 2014. Raised a $2.5M seed (Nov 2015, Octopus lead) and a $5.3M/£4M Series A (Oct 2017, Octopus lead). Acquired by Kaplan (agreed March 2020, announced Jan 2021, undisclosed) and later by Manifest Global (2025).

companies.name: Satago
companies.description: Helping businesses get paid on time.
companies.funding_notes: Satago (satago.com) is a London invoice-finance and credit-control platform for SMEs; TruFin plc is its majority owner. Raised £30K on Seedrs, a $1M 'second round' in May 2014 (E-merge, BDMI, Ed Wray, William Reeve), and £1.6M equity from ESF Capital in June 2016 alongside a £3M credit line (debt, excluded), plus £550K from previous investors. Lloyds took a 20% stake for £5M in March 2022 (£20M pre-money). Reputable sources never give these equity rounds a stage label (some databases call the 2016 deal a Series A), hence unclear-round-type. Mixed USD/GBP; GBP equity is ~£7.18M plus $1M.

companies.name: Oradian
companies.description: Oradian provides a unique enterprise solution to financial institutions across South East Asia and Africa.
companies.funding_notes: Oradian (oradian.com) is a Zagreb-based cloud core-banking (Instafin) provider for microfinance institutions in Africa and the Philippines. TechCrunch reported an undisclosed seed round in May 2015 (Credo, Playfair, Day One, Esther Dyson, Africa Angels Network); Seedcamp is named as another seed investor. A $2.1M Series A (July 2016, Rivers Capital Partners lead, with Finance in Motion) comes from Poslovni dnevnik, which itself cites a database, so treat the amount with caution. Feb 2018 investments from Middleton Enterprises (~100K, currency garbled in source) and Goodwell were undisclosed. Total unknown, so amount_raised is blank.

companies.name: Elliptic
companies.description: Identifying illicit activity on the blockchain

funding_rounds.stage: Funding round (unlabelled; databases list as Seed)

companies.funding_notes: Elliptic (elliptic.co) is a London blockchain analytics / crypto compliance company founded 2013 that joined Seedcamp in Feb 2014. Raised $2M from Octopus (Jul 2014), $5M Series A led by Paladin (Mar 2018), a Series B that opened at $23M led by SBI (Sep 2019) and grew to $28M with Wells Fargo Strategic Capital (May 2020), and a $60M Series C led by Evolution Equity with SoftBank Vision Fund 2 (Oct 2021). Total ~$95M.

companies.name: Tanaza
companies.description: All-in-one software that turns common Wi-Fi routers into cloud-managed Wi-Fi social hotspots.

grants.name: European Commission (Horizon 2020 SME Instrument Phase 2 / EIC)

companies.funding_notes: Tanaza (tanaza.com) is a Milan-based cloud Wi-Fi management software company (Tanaza SpA). Early financing came from Italian investment firm OrmaPrima; it joined Seedcamp in Feb 2014. A '€500K seed led by Seedcamp' figure appears only in aggregator databases and is not confirmed by reputable press. Got a €1.62M Horizon 2020 SME Instrument grant (signed Jul 2019); Il Sole 24 Ore (Aug 2019) said a third-party investor might come in within 6-12 months, but no later priced round was found.

companies.name: Fishbrain
companies.description: The fastest growing app & social network for the world's biggest hobby - sport fishing
companies.funding_notes: Fishbrain (fishbrain.com) is a Stockholm-based fishing app, social network and marketplace that won Seedcamp Berlin in 2013. Rounds: $150K seed (2013), $2.4M pre-Series A (2014, Northzone/Active), $8M Series A (2015, Northzone), $13.5M Series B (2018, B Capital; TechCrunch said total $28M by then), and an unlabelled $31M round (Mar 2021). A 2022 Republic SPV listing (withdrawn) describes a $20M Series C at a $70M pre-money valuation; that close isn't independently confirmed, so its amount is not counted. amount_raised sums the listed rounds; TechCrunch's total implies ~$59M including earlier undisclosed money.

companies.name: Countly
companies.description: Mobile analytics for the enterprise
companies.funding_notes: Countly (countly.com) is an open-source, self-hosted product analytics platform founded by Onur Alp Soner. It was picked at Mini Seedcamp Istanbul in 2013 and joined Seedcamp (undisclosed micro-investment), but the CEO says it has been bootstrapped and took no outside VC. A '£830K seed led by Seedcamp' on StartupHub.ai mixes it up with London-based Count (Sifted, May 2026) and is excluded.

companies.name: Codacy
companies.description: Automating code reviews and monitors code quality over time.
companies.funding_notes: Codacy (codacy.com) is a Lisbon-based automated code review / code quality platform that went through Seedcamp. Raised a €1M ($1.1M) seed extension in Oct 2015 led by Caixa Capital (total €1.5M then, so ~€0.5M in earlier undisclosed seed money), a $5.1M Series A in Aug 2017 led by EQT Ventures with Seedcamp, and a $15M Series B in Sep 2022 led by Bright Pixel. amount_raised ($21.2M) leaves out the earlier ~€0.5M.

companies.name: James Finance
companies.description: Predict bad loans with Machine Learning. Based on the best machine learning algorithms, James helps Risk Officers generate highly predictive credit scoring models.
companies.funding_notes: James (james.finance, formerly CrowdProcess) was a Lisbon/New York credit-risk ML startup founded 2011 by João Menano, Pedro Fonseca and Sam Hopkins; Seedcamp invested after Seedcamp Lisbon in Nov 2012. In June/July 2017 it raised $2.7M (€2.5M), led by ex-Credit Suisse board member Gaël de Boissard with Henry Ritchotte and BiG Start Ventures; sources don't give it a stage label. Reportedly acquired by Google in January 2019 (database/Portuguese press; terms undisclosed).

companies.name: Codeship
companies.description: A fast and secure hosted Continuous Delivery platform that scales with your needs.
companies.funding_notes: Codeship (codeship.com) was a hosted CI/CD platform founded in Vienna in 2011 by Moritz Plassnig, Manuel Weiss and Florian Motlik, later based in Boston (Techstars Boston alum). Raised $2.6M in Feb 2014 led by Sigma Prime (unlabelled in VentureBeat) and a $7M Series A in July 2016 led by Ascent Venture Partners (total $11.1M per Business Wire, so ~$1.5M earlier money is undisclosed). CloudBees acquired it in Feb 2018, terms undisclosed.

companies.name: Minubo
companies.description: eCommerce Intelligence in the Cloud. Your online shop’s data hub with all key metrics
companies.funding_notes: minubo.com (minubo GmbH), Hamburg, Germany; e-commerce BI SaaS, founded 2013, opened Boston office (minubo Inc.) in 2014. €1M seed Sep 2013 (Seedcamp, Tola Capital, HTGF + e-commerce angels) per TechCrunch/HTGF; second seed Dec 2014 described only as 'seven-digit', led by Stephan Schambach with Seedcamp, HTGF, Tola (EU-Startups/HTGF). Total left blank because second round amount is undisclosed (at least ~€2M combined). No later equity round found in reputable sources; trackers mention later debt/secondary only.

companies.name: Hole19
companies.description: Building the most amazing user experience for golfers on the course!

grants.name: Prémio Nacional de Indústrias Criativas (Fundação de Serralves / Unicer)

companies.funding_notes: hole19golf.com, Lisbon, Portugal; golf GPS/scorecard app founded 2011 by Anthony Douglas; Seedcamp 2013. Forbes Portugal: White Star Capital and e42 invested €170k after Seedcamp (2013); second round 2014 with Faber Ventures of 'close to €300k' (amount left null as approximate); founder also used family/friends money, a €25k creative-industries prize and applied for €500k QREN funding (QREN grant receipt implied, not explicitly confirmed). Observador later cited ~€2.2M invested by Faber, Caixa Capital, White Star, e42, Seedcamp and angels. The Aug 2017 ~€3.47M round (Caixa Capital, Kibo, White Star, Faber) is sourced only from tracker-style sites (bouncewatch/indexed; amounts vary $1.7M–$4.1M) — no reputable press article found. White Star Capital lists Hole19 as an active portfolio company. Total left blank given conflicting/approximate figures.

companies.name: SimpleTax
companies.description: The smart self assessment tax return filing software
companies.funding_notes: gosimpletax.com (GoSimpleTax), UK self-assessment tax filing software. Original SimpleTax was founded by Portuguese CEO Celso Pinto, attended Seedcamp Week London Sep 2012 and got Seedcamp funding (accelerator check, amount undisclosed), launched in UK Jan 2013 (TNW). A ~£150k Dec 2012 seed appears only on tracker sites. Caveat: AccountingWEB describes today's GoSimpleTax as founded 2016 by the team behind Keytime, so ownership appears to have changed hands (transfer not publicly documented). Only public financing found: £250k DEBT from NPIF – FW Capital Debt Finance (Oct 2022) — debt, not equity, so not counted. GoSimpleTax acquired Coconut (bookkeeping app) in 2023. No priced equity round found.

companies.name: SayDuck
companies.description: Add reality to your sales
companies.funding_notes: sayduck.com, Helsinki, Finland (office in Vilnius); 3D/AR product visualization for e-commerce, founded 2012. ArcticStartup: €350k seed (Jan 2014) from IncubAsia Ventures, Arteel Ventures and angels; another €350k (Nov 2014) led by Arteel. ~€1.2M total incl. Seedcamp €50k and a €450k 2013 round per Tech.eu Funding Explorer (data product; 2013 round not confirmed in a news article). ACQUIRED by Bublar Group (Sweden) July 2019 for SEK 13.5M paid in newly issued Bublar shares plus an earn-out (Cision). Later part of Goodbye Kansas Group; Dealroom says it partnered with The Optical Foundry in 2024 (unverified).

companies.name: Antavo
companies.description: Contest and loyalty software for e-commerce and retail brands
companies.funding_notes: antavo.com, London-registered with HQ/engineering in Szeged, Hungary; enterprise loyalty cloud SaaS (clients BMW, KFC, BrewDog). €10M Series A Nov 2022 led by Euroventures with Lead Ventures, iEurope, Innovation Nest and angels (PR Newswire/Tech.eu). EIB story: €1.3M investment from Innovation Nest in 2018 (iEurope reportedly co-invested; seed label from trackers). Total €11.3M = sum of these two sourced rounds; small earlier Seedcamp/angel rounds (2012-2016) are undisclosed. Company said in Sep 2024 it was preparing a Series B for 2025; no completed Series B found.

companies.name: 24Symbols
companies.description: Read digital books online
companies.funding_notes: 24symbols.com, Madrid, Spain; 'Spotify for ebooks' subscription reading platform founded 2010, Seedcamp portfolio. May 2013: mobile content group Zed bought a 32% stake for €2M (implied €6.25M valuation) alongside a distribution deal (TNW, independently confirmed; madri+d). Stage never named — a corporate strategic minority investment, hence unclear-round-type. An earlier ~€250k round is mentioned only in secondary coverage (El Cronista), not counted. Status today uncertain: site/apps still up, but Draft2Digital removed 24symbols distribution in Jan 2021 citing operational/payment problems — possibly dormant.

companies.name: Qminder
companies.description: Qminder is a cloud-based queue management system.

investors: angels from Toggl, Veriff, Pipedrive, Wise, Twilio

companies.funding_notes: qminder.com, Tartu, Estonia; queue/service-flow management SaaS founded 2011 (Garage48 origin), Seedcamp-backed 2012, then ~10 years profitable bootstrapping (small 2014 angel investment from Astrec Invest per trackers, undisclosed). €3M seed Nov 2024 led by Practica Capital with Jaan Tallinn's Metaplanet, BADideas.fund and angels — described by the company as its first institutional funding (Qminder blog, Tech.eu). Total reflects only this round.
notable_investors: angels from Toggl, Veriff, Pipedrive, Wise, Twilio

companies.name: Wise
companies.description: Send money abroad easily and quickly with low-cost transfers
companies.funding_notes: wise.com (Wise plc, formerly TransferWise), London; founded 2011 by Taavet Hinrikus and Kristo Käärmann; Seedcamp was a pre-seed/seed investor (sold its stake by 2017). Sourced rounds: $6M Series A 2013 (Valar), $25M Series B 2014 (Branson), $58M Series C 2015 (a16z), $280M Series E Nov 2017 (Old Mutual GI + IVP, ~$1.6B valuation, partly secondary). TechCrunch: total raised $397M as of Nov 2017 (includes a 2016 Series D not itemized here, and some secondary). Later 2019/2020 rounds were largely secondary share sales and not counted. PUBLIC: direct listing on the London Stock Exchange 7 Jul 2021, ~£8.75B (~$11B) valuation (Reuters/CNBC).

companies.name: Holvi
companies.description: Banking for makers and doers
companies.funding_notes: holvi.com, Helsinki, Finland; online business banking for freelancers/SMEs founded 2011, Seedcamp-backed. €1M round May 2014 led by Speedinvest (its first Nordic deal) to expand to Austria/Ireland (ArcticStartup/Finovate) — labelled seed by trackers. Tech.eu: ~€2M raised in total before ACQUISITION by BBVA (Mar 2016, terms undisclosed). BBVA sold Holvi in Feb 2021 to Keru Fintech Investments, a vehicle of co-founder Tuomas Toivonen (management buyback); profitable by 2023. Dealroom lists additional small 2011-2015 rounds (€300k-€2.5M) not confirmed in press; total uses Tech.eu's ~€2M figure.

companies.name: Grabcad
companies.description: GrabCAD is an online community network for mechanical engineers to share talent, expand knowledge and collaborate with others.
companies.funding_notes: grabcad.com, Boston (Estonian roots/dev office in Tallinn); online CAD community and collaboration platform. TechCrunch Oct 2012: $8.15M Series B led by Charles River Ventures with David Sacks and existing Atlas, NextView, Matrix; prior $1.1M seed and $4M Series A (dates not given there); TC says ~$14M total — $13.25M is the sum of the three disclosed rounds. ACQUIRED by Stratasys (all-cash, closed 23 Sep 2014; ~ $100M reported, terms not officially disclosed). Now part of Stratasys.

companies.name: Profitero
companies.description: Global Online Insights for Retailers and Brands
companies.funding_notes: profitero.com, founded 2010 in Dublin (Dún Laoghaire), Ireland, offices in Boston/NY/London etc.; e-commerce analytics. $8M Series A Jun 2014 from Polaris Partners (TechCrunch/company PR); $20M Series B Apr 2020 led by Scaleworks with Conviction Capital (Irish Times/company PR). Irish Times: total 'more than $30M' including ~$9M from Polaris + Silicon Valley Bank and ~$1M early seed from Delta Partners and Enterprise Ireland — amount_raised uses that $30M floor. ACQUIRED by Publicis Groupe May 2022 for €200M (Reuters).

companies.name: EDITED
companies.description: The world’s biggest apparel data warehouse.
companies.funding_notes: edited.com, London (also Dallas, Sofia); retail intelligence/apparel data SaaS founded 2009 by Geoff Watts and Julia Fowler. $29M round Apr 2020 led by Wavecrest Growth Partners and Beringea UK with Hermes, bringing total to $34M (VentureBeat); $15M growth round Mar 2023 led by Delta-v Capital (company press, Tech.eu). Total $49M = $34M + $15M. Round labels are 'growth'; no Series letter published.

companies.name: Scoville
companies.description: A location-based recommendation engine that helps users discover at least one new place in their town each week
companies.funding_notes: goscoville.com (also scoville.com), London; location-discovery app built on Foursquare check-ins (#TopTuesday), pivoted from travel startup Kukunu; founders Gerald Goldstein and Itamar Lesuisse. TechCrunch Apr 2011: 'recently raised $400K in funding from Seedcamp, Kima Ventures, and Jaina Capital', called seed funding — small and round terms (priced vs convertible) unknown; includes the Seedcamp check, so seed+ is borderline. No later funding or activity found; appears DEFUNCT (domain could not be confirmed live).

companies.name: Erply
companies.description: Web based affordable point of sale software and inventory system for retailers
companies.funding_notes: erply.com, Estonia (Tallinn) with US presence (NYC sales office in 2013); cloud POS/inventory software for retailers, CEO Kristjan Hiiemaa. $2M Mar 2010 from Redpoint, Index Ventures and angels (TechCrunch, Ärileht); $2.15M Series B May 2013 led by Redpoint with Index and 500 Startups, TechCrunch says total VC $4.2M (sum of disclosed rounds $4.15M; small early Seedcamp ~€50k 2009 check not counted). A ~€50k EU Horizon 2020 SME grant (2016) is mentioned only by trackers, not included. No later round found; company still operating.

companies.name: Codility
companies.description: Codility is an automated tool for assessment of programming skills.
companies.funding_notes: Codility (codility.com; Codility Limited, Companies House 07048726), Warsaw-founded technical-skills assessment platform with London/San Francisco offices. Seedcamp 2009 winner (EUR 50k for a 5-10% stake), then bootstrapped for ~10 years before a $22M Series A in Jan 2020 co-led by Oxx and Kennet Partners. Companies House SH01 shows Series B preferred shares allotted for cash 4-14 Jul 2022 totalling ~GBP 28.9M (computed from shares x price paid); investors and any press announcement for this Series B were not found, so investors are left empty. amount_raised left blank because rounds are in mixed EUR/USD/GBP (~$22M + ~GBP 28.9M + EUR 50k).

companies.name: Platogo
companies.description: Gaming studio
companies.funding_notes: Platogo (platogo.com), Vienna-based browser/social game portal and studio (launched Sept 2009, user-generated game levels). Seedcamp invested via a Mini Seedcamp event in 2009 (amount undisclosed, per TechCrunch); the Guardian reports funding from departure, Vienna city council's entrepreneurial fund (treated as public funding/grant, amount undisclosed). No priced seed or VC round found. Later became a subsidiary of Greentube (Novomatic's interactive division), per Greentube's own publications; the ~2013 acquisition date comes only from trackers.

companies.name: Patients Know Best
companies.description: Patients Know Best provide hospitals with personal health records software so that their patients can better manage their health
companies.funding_notes: Patients Know Best (patientsknowbest.com), Cambridge/London UK patient-controlled personal health record platform (founder/CEO Dr Mohammad Al-Ubaydli), B Corp. Seedcamp 2009 winner (EUR 50k). Raised $1.7M led by Maxfield Capital (Nov 2014; company later called it GBP 1m), GBP 3.5m led by Balderton Capital (Dec 2015), an undisclosed equity round led by OMRON Ventures with Balderton (Jun 2019) and an undisclosed strategic minority investment from DNV Ventures (Sep 2025). None of these is given a seed/Series label in primary or reputable sources (trackers label 2019 a Series A), hence unclear-round-type even though they are VC-led. A GBP 6m facility from Growth Lending (reported by Digital Health) is a loan and is excluded from rounds and totals. amount_raised blank: mixed EUR/USD/GBP and two undisclosed rounds.

companies.name: toksta
companies.description: Highly scalable instant messenger and chat solutions for online communities
companies.funding_notes: toksta (toksta.com), Berlin/Potsdam white-label instant messaging and webcam chat for online communities, founded late 2007 by Felix Fidelsberger and Michael Gloess; later renamed stickapps. Seedcamp 2008 winner (EUR 50k) and also backed by Team Europe Ventures (amount and round type undisclosed). Sold in Dec 2009 to Roman Szubryt (owner of Polish dev shop Mainseek), per deutsche-startups.de; terms undisclosed. The domain is now defunct. amount_raised shows the disclosed Seedcamp EUR 50k only.

companies.name: stupeflix
companies.description: Make beautiful videos online, easily
companies.funding_notes: Stupeflix (stupeflix.com), Paris-based online/mobile video creation company (Stupeflix Studio, API, Replay and Steady apps). Seedcamp 2008 winner (EUR 50k); TechCrunch (Jul 2014) says it had 'barely raised money', from Seedcamp and 500 Startups (500 Startups amount, date and round type undisclosed; trackers date it to Nov 2012 alongside Andurance Ventures and angels, not confirmed in reputable sources). GoPro acquired Stupeflix and Vemory in Feb 2016 for $105M combined (cash and stock). amount_raised shows the disclosed Seedcamp EUR 50k only.

companies.name: Evercontact
companies.description: Your contacts automatically up to date

investors: Private investors advised by Financiere Fonds Prives

companies.funding_notes: Evercontact (evercontact.com), Paris-based service that extracts contact details from email signatures to keep address books/CRMs up to date; built by Kwaga (formerly WriteThat.Name). Seedcamp invested via a Mini Seedcamp in 2009 and Kima Ventures also provided early seed money (amounts undisclosed). Raised a $1.55M Series A from private investors advised by Financiere Fonds Prives (Jan 2012) and $1M (~EUR 700k) from AXA Strategic Ventures (Apr 2015, AXA's first investment; stage unlabelled). amount_raised = disclosed USD rounds only ($1.55M + $1M).
notable_investors: Private investors advised by Financiere Fonds Prives

companies.name: Basekit
companies.description: The most partner friendly site builder
companies.funding_notes: BaseKit (basekit.com), Bristol/London-based white-label website builder sold through hosting and telco partners (founders Simon Best, Richard Best, Richard Healy). Seedcamp 2008 winner (EUR 50k); $2.6M Series A from Eden Ventures and NESTA (Jun 2010); $6.5M (~GBP 4M) from Nauta Capital, Eden and NESTA (Mar 2011); GBP 4.5m led by Angel CoFund (Feb 2014), which TechCrunch said brought the total to ~GBP 14.5m; and GBP 1m from existing investors (Mar 2022). That implies ~GBP 15.5m total, but amount_raised is left blank because the rounds mix EUR/USD/GBP. An undisclosed 2009 Eden/NESTA investment appears in secondary sources only.

companies.name: Zemanta
companies.description: Content Ads, Amplified & Optimized
companies.funding_notes: Zemanta (zemanta.com), Ljubljana, Slovenia-founded company (later HQ'd in New York) that started as a blogging recommendation tool and became a native-advertising DSP (Zemanta One). Seedcamp 2007 winner. Seed money from Eden Ventures and The Accelerator Group, then Union Square Ventures added $650k in Sep 2008 (TechCrunch: $2.2M seed raised to that point from the three); $3M from USV and Eden (Nov 2010, ~$6M total); $2M from USV and Social Starts (Nov 2013). The company said it had raised $8M to date, which is used as amount_raised (Tech.eu later said 'more than $8 million'). A $1.6M Aug 2009 round appears only in trackers and is not itemised. Outbrain acquired Zemanta in Jul 2017 (undisclosed).

companies.name: MyBuilder
companies.description: Find trusted builders and tradesmen.
companies.funding_notes: MyBuilder (mybuilder.com), London-based marketplace matching homeowners with vetted tradespeople, founded by former stonemason Ryan Notz (began as Buildersite in 2004). Seedcamp 2007 winner, then undisclosed angel money; profitable in 2008. Channel 4's 4iP fund bought a GBP 350k minority stake in Sep 2009 (not given a round label). IAC's HomeAdvisor acquired MyBuilder in Mar 2017 (terms undisclosed); Angi later raised its stake to 95% in 2021. amount_raised shows the disclosed GBP 350k only (Seedcamp and angel amounts undisclosed).

companies.name: Lupin & Holmes
companies.description: Offensive security for software supply-chain risk

investors: founders of Wiz, Hugging Face and GitGuardian (angels)

companies.funding_notes: Lupin & Holmes (landh.tech), founded by bug bounty hunter Roni Carta, builds Depi for software supply-chain offensive security. Raised a $5.9M pre-seed (Tech.eu, 2026-03-17) co-led by 20VC and Seedcamp with Purple Fund, Kima Ventures and angel founders of Wiz, Hugging Face and GitGuardian. No seed or later round found.
notable_investors: founders of Wiz, Hugging Face and GitGuardian (angels)

companies.name: Crowd.dev
companies.description: Developer community data platform

investors: angels (Russ Heddleston, Cedric Sellin, Matthäus Krzykowski, Christian Stiebner)

companies.funding_notes: Verified crowd.dev. Berlin developer-community data platform (Jonathan Reimer, Joan). Raised €2.2M pre-seed announced late Oct 2022 co-led by Seedcamp and Lightbird (company DEV post / Seedcamp / TechCrunch). Acquired by the Linux Foundation (founder announcement ~2024-04-15/17); code now under linuxfoundation/crowd.dev. No seed or later equity round found before the acquisition.
notable_investors: angels (Russ Heddleston, Cedric Sellin, Matthäus Krzykowski, Christian Stiebner)

companies.name: Rosita
companies.description: AI-based longevity coach, specifically built for seniors
companies.funding_notes: Rosita Longevity (rositalongevity.com; legal entity Hearts Radiant), Spanish startup from Cofrentes, Valencia, founded 2020, expanding to Florida. €450k pre-seed (Oct 2020) led by JME.vc (PlantaDoce reports €430k); €2.4M (~$2.8M) seed (Feb 2022) led by Ship2B Ventures. Total ~€2.85M.

companies.name: kitch
companies.description: The virtual food market for restaurants to win in the digital age
companies.funding_notes: kitch.io verified (Kitch Technologies, Lisbon, Portugal; restaurant delivery/online-store platform launched Mar 2020, CEO Rui Bento). €1M pre-seed (2020) from initial investors Seedcamp and Mustard Seed MAZE (per Seedcamp; exact date not confirmed), then €3.25M (~$4M) seed (May 2021) led by Atlantic Food Labs with Market One Capital, Seedcamp and Mustard Seed MAZE. No later rounds found.

companies.name: Skew
companies.description: Building a crypto derivatives analytics & trading platform for the institutional market
companies.funding_notes: skew.com: London crypto derivatives analytics & trading platform (co-founders Emmanuel Goh, Tim Noat). $2M seed (Sep 2019, FirstMinute/Seedcamp; CoinDesk headline also named Kleiner Perkins though body listed FirstMinute lead). $5M follow-on (Apr 2020, Octopus) totaling $7M. Coinbase announced acquisition Apr 2021 (closed ~Q2 2021); deal value not published. Domain verified; now part of Coinbase institutional stack.

companies.name: Speechly
companies.description: Spoken language understanding API for developers
companies.funding_notes: Domain speechly.com matches (Helsinki). Acquired by Roblox in Sept 2023 (Roblox SEC filing; ~$10.1M incl. contingent consideration). Tracker-only (Seedtable) 2022 $500k pre-seed and $125k entries excluded as unverified.

companies.name: Parla
companies.description: Revolutionising reproductive health by providing greater access to diagnostic tests and proactive support
companies.funding_notes: Assumed to be Parla, the AI-powered English-teacher app (launched 2017; Seedcamp portfolio). Could not confirm the myparla.com domain: site timed out and archive lookups failed; appears defunct (trackers say ceased operations). EUR2M 2017 raise from Oleg Gutsol is from a single Russian-language aggregator (Rusvest), no stage given, unverified. Seedcamp + London Co-Investment Fund investment (2018) known only from trackers (Nordic9 no amount; Dealroom £250k 'seed'), so excluded from rounds. Not a priced seed in primary sources.

companies.name: Fleksy
companies.description: Text input SDKs, enabling developers to create outstanding typing products
companies.funding_notes: Fleksy (fleksy.com), Barcelona keyboard/text-input SDK company operated by ThingThing (Seedcamp portfolio Jan 2016, CEO Olivier Plante), which acquired the Fleksy keyboard assets in 2017. €350k (~$400k) seed as Thingthing (May 2016), $815k equity crowdfund (Oct 2018) and $1.6M Series A led by Inveready (Oct 2021); TechCrunch says just under $3M (€2.5M) raised in total. The original US Fleksy maker Syntellia's rounds ($3M Series A 2013, $2M 2014) belong to a different entity and are excluded.

companies.name: Lateral
companies.description: Automating Information Discovery
companies.funding_notes: Lateral (lateral.io), Berlin machine-intelligence information/research discovery tool. Went through Deutsche Telekom's hub:raum accelerator (2014) and received a Seedcamp investment (Dec 2014, undisclosed). A €300k 2014 raise appears only in Dealroom (not primary). No priced seed+ round found. Lateral was sunset on 26 June 2025 (team moving to coordination.network).

companies.name: Pointy
companies.description: The simple way for local shops to get online and attract more customers through their door.
companies.funding_notes: Pointy (pointy.com), Dublin startup putting local retailers' in-store inventory online via a POS-connected box/app. $1.2m seed (LocalGlobe, Frontline, Seedcamp; date not given), $6m Series A (Sep 2017), $12m Series B led by Polaris (Jul 2018); Silicon Republic put total at ~$19m. Acquired by Google, announced Jan 2020 (~€147m/$163m per TechCrunch source).

companies.name: ShareLaTex
companies.description: Easy-to-use, online, collaborative LaTex editor
companies.funding_notes: ShareLaTeX (sharelatex.com, Scribtex Ltd) was a London online collaborative LaTeX editor founded by Henry Oswald and James Allen. Its only public external funding is Seedcamp's undisclosed micro-seed investment after Seedcamp Week London in Sept 2013; it was revenue-generating. Overleaf (backed by Digital Science) fully acquired it in July 2017 and the products were merged.

companies.name: Server Density
companies.description: Server Monitoring Built For Security And Scale
companies.funding_notes: Server Density (serverdensity.com), UK SaaS server/infrastructure monitoring company founded 2009 by David Mytton and Harry Wincup (originally Boxed Ice, a Seedcamp 2009 winner). Took EUR 50k from Seedcamp, then undisclosed angel money (Christoph Janz, Dick Williams, Qamar Aziz), then a $1.5M seed round led by SP Ventures (TechCrunch, Dec 2015); otherwise largely bootstrapped. Merged into/acquired by StackPath in May 2018 (terms undisclosed). amount_raised blank because rounds mix EUR and USD (EUR 50k + $1.5M + undisclosed angel money).

companies.name: Talasim
companies.description: An online comedy channel providing a space for self-expression and humour
companies.funding_notes: Talasim (talasim.com), Amman, Jordan-based Arabic online comedy/user-generated humour site founded by Zeid Koudsi and Sabri Hakim. The input website jeeran.com belongs to Jeeran, the Jordanian online community portal (co-founded by Zeid's brother Omar Koudsi) that hosted Talasim's original blog, made an early investment in it (amount undisclosed) and then acquired it. Seedcamp 2009 winner (EUR 50k for a 5-10% stake). Jeeran acquired Talasim and its engineering team in Mar 2010 for $1M in Jeeran stock (The National). No priced seed round. amount_raised shows the disclosed Seedcamp EUR 50k only.

companies.name: ubervu
companies.description: Insights-driven social analytics
companies.funding_notes: uberVU (ubervu.com), social media monitoring/analytics company founded by Romanians Vladimir Oane, Dragos Ilinca and Dan Ciotu; founded in London in 2008, later HQ'd in Boston, with engineering in Bucharest. Seedcamp 2008 winner (EUR 50k), then a second round from an Eden Ventures-managed fund signed in Jan 2009 (founder told startups.ro it was 'up to EUR 1M'; trackers say EUR 400k; round type not stated). TechCrunch (Jan 2014) says it raised 'a very modest $586,000' in total, which is used as amount_raised. HootSuite acquired it in Jan 2014 (undisclosed; TechCrunch heard $15-20M).

companies.name: rentmineonline
companies.description: Connecting Trusted Owners and Renters.
companies.funding_notes: RentMineOnline (rentmineonline.com), San Francisco-based SaaS for multifamily rental marketing through resident referrals on social networks and email (CEO Ed Spiegel), founded 2007. 451 Research lists backers fbFund, Partners in Equity, Seedcamp and Alex Hoye (ex-GoIndustry CEO); amounts, dates and round types are undisclosed (trackers date the Seedcamp check to 2007 and fbFund to Jun 2009; fbFund deals were small grant/seed-style checks). RealPage acquired it in Jul 2012 for ~$6.0M at closing plus up to $3.5M contingent on revenue milestones (~$1.5M trailing revenue).
